summary:
Allwork.Space reports that after a year of federal workforce reductions, the Trump administration is pivoting toward expanded hiring in targeted areas, especially early-career workers and technology talent.

An Office of Personnel Management (OPM) memo directs agencies to build fiscal 2027 staffing plans prioritizing younger employees, IT professionals, and other mission-critical roles. OPM wants at least 33% of all FY2027 federal hires to be early-career employees. Agencies are encouraged to recruit via programs including Pathways, the CyberAICorps Scholarship for Service, and a new early-career talent network on USAJobs. The administration is also expanding its Tech Force initiative, targeting roughly 1,000 technologists in two-year federal positions, with about 300 already onboard.

The push follows deep staffing cuts. Since early 2025 the federal workforce has shrunk by roughly 271,600 employees through departures and constrained hiring, per Federal News Network. OPM is using shared hiring pools to help agencies refill roles hit hardest by losses, including project managers, HR professionals, IT specialists, financial management specialists, and contract specialists.

To streamline hiring, agencies are being urged to use shared candidate lists and technical skills assessments, and to recruit beyond the Washington, D.C. area. Agencies such as the Department of Veterans Affairs, CISA, the CDC, and the State Department have outlined hiring plans.

Despite the recruitment drive, overall federal hiring remains well below prior levels: USAJobs postings fell nearly 43% between 2024 and 2025, and federal employment continued to decline in June 2026.

The piece is a public-sector labor market and hiring policy story. It does not address workplace technology topics such as visitor management, desk or room booking, hybrid or return-to-office policy mechanics, workplace analytics, or facilities operations, so it offers little direct relevance to workplace experience buyers beyond context on federal headcount trends.
